text: Sri Chautaria Fateh Jang Shah, also known as Fatya Jang Shah or Fatte Jang Chautariya, served as the 6th prime minister of Nepal. Born in 1805, he was the eldest son of Sri Chautaria Prana Shah and Chautaryani Moha Kumari Devi, belonging to the 6th generation of King Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha. He was the nephew of Prime Minister Chautariya Pushkar Shah and had four brothers: Colonel Sri Chautaria Guru Prasad Shah, Rajguru Ram Krishna Bahadur Shah, Captain Sardar Bir Bahadur Shah, and Colonel Sri Chautaria Rana Sher Shah. His sister was Hiranya Garbha Devi, who became the third wife of Prime Minister Jung Bahadur Rana. Fateh Jung Shah received private education. He was appointed Mukhtiyar from 1840 to 1843 and lived in exile at Gaya, India from 1843 to 1845. In 1845, after his exile, he was promoted to Full General and Commander of Three Regiments. He then served as Mukhtiyar and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1845 to 1846. He had three sons: Sri Chautaria Khadga Bikram Shah (Khadga Babusaheb), who was killed with him during the Kot Massacre on 14 September 1846, and Guru Prasad Shah and Guna Bahadur Shah. Fateh Jung Shah was killed in the Kot Massacre at the courtyard of Hanuman Dhoka Palace on 14 September 1846.
